title: Windows x64 long and pointer widths are different
summary: Windows x64 uses LLP64, longs are usually 32 bits and pointers are 64 bits; both are 64 bits in common 64-bit Unix LP64.
applies: 64-bit native ABI; interprets types and calls based on build target
detail: The same structure containing long writes the memory image directly from both ends, and the field offsets may be different. Use fixed-width external fields for stable parsing.
boundary: You can't tell the width of long just by knowing that the machine is x86-64.
relevance: Explain why two 64-bit builds write records of different lengths.
